title: Why your blood can fizz like soda 🫧
subject: astronaut
description:
Would you sit in a spacesuit for 4 hours to avoid this? 👇

What is decompression sickness, or the bends? When pressure drops too fast, nitrogen dissolved in your body forms bubbles. It's why NASA astronauts breathe pure oxygen before spacewalks.

Sources: NASA Office of the Chief Health & Medical Officer, Decompression Sickness Technical Brief (OCHMO-TB-037)
tags: what happens if you surface too fast

scenes.text: Your blood can fizz like a freshly opened soda.
Under pressure, nitrogen dissolves into your body. Drop the pressure too fast, and it comes out as bubbles.
It's called the bends: aching joints, itching, sometimes numbness.
Spacewalks carry the same risk. The International Space Station is kept at 14.7 psi. NASA's spacesuit runs at 4.3.
So in one method, an astronaut sits in the suit for 4 hours breathing pure oxygen.
NASA has never had a case reach an astronaut's nervous system in space.
